edits.value_json: Lila handed Moss the paper crown. “For a guest,” she said. Moss lowered his head, and the crown settled between his ears. His proud ears stood even prouder.
At the hilltop, Tomas rang the brass bell for Juniper. Its bright notes skipped down the green slope and over the waiting wagon, sounding like tiny golden footsteps.
At the hilltop, the brass bell sent tiny notes tumbling down the sunny slope toward the waiting wagon. Aunt Juniper smiled beneath the wide blue sky, and the hill seemed to smile back.
The brass bell sang above the hilltop, its little notes rolling down the green slope like shiny marbles. Aunt Juniper laughed at the top while the bright day gathered around her.
